MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 20, 2026
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Villablanca called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Judy Villablanca; Vice Chair Jake Lingo; Commissioners Alicia Peak
  (arrived at 6:39 p.m.), and Dane Skophammer

  ABSENT: Commissioner Georgia Goldfarb

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Kate Manisco,
  Recreation Manager; Chris Orosz, Interim Recreation Manager; Brittany Saleaumua,
  Administrative Assistant; and Alexandra Elizondo, Regular Part-Time Permanent

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Villablanca led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Vice Chair Lingo seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 3—0;
  Commissioners Goldfarb and Peak absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on January 15, 2026.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Special Events Presentation

  Recreation Manager Manisco introduced Regular Part-Time Permanent Alexandra
  Elizondo who presented an overview of the special events coordinated by the
  Community Services Department.

  Commissioner Peak arrived at 6:39 p.m.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Scott Dittrich proposed a dog park at Las Flores Creek Park on Rambla Paciflco
  Street.

  Bonnie Decker stated Trancas Riders and Ropers were interested in working with
  the City to assist in maintaining Malibu Equestrian Park and requested to finalize a
  Community Use Agreement.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Lingo moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to approve
  the consent calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Goldfarb absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  l.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the October 21, 2025
  Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in November and December 2025.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Jake Kurediian Citizenship Award
  Recommended Action: Discuss the nomination process for the 2026 Jake
  Kuredjian Citizenship Award.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  Chair Villablanca recommended opening the nomination process to the public.

  Vice Chair Lingo indicated agreement with Chair Villablanca.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of January 20, 2026
  Page 3 of 6

  Commissioner Skophammer recommended Gina McCloskey and Bonnie Decker
  for their involvement with Trancas Riders and Ropers, and Denise de Garmo, a
  wildlife specialist.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the public
  nomination process would be advertised on social media, the website, and in the
  Malibu Times.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
  award could be presented at a Parks and Recreation Commission meeting after it
  had been presented to the recipient at a City Council meeting.

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Vice Chair Lingo seconded a motion to open the
  public nomination period for the 2026 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award and
  recognize the 2026 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award recipient at a future Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting. The question was called, and the
  motion carried 4-0; Commissioner Goldfarb absent.

  Request for Qualifications for Recreation Programs
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Request for Qualifications criteria for
  recreation program proposals; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the Request
  for Qualifications (RFQ) was released when two instructors were interested in
  providing the same program.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  instructors would certify that their proposals are accurate when submitting them for
  review. She stated additional fact checking could be done during the RFQ process.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Recreation Manager Manisco stated certain sports
  or programs would require professional certifications.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco stated
  that the 2024 Aquatics (Swim Team) RFQ proposals were reviewed by members
  of the Southern California Public Pool Operators Association.

  Commissioner Peak stated the proposal grading rubric should be straightforward.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated industry professionals were selected for the
  panel to review and evaluate the proposals.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of January 20, 2026
  Page 4 of 6

Commissioner Peak stated grading metrics should be clearly outlined so applicants
can understand how a proposal was graded.

Community Services Director Riesgo stated that a grading rubric was given to the
RFQ review panel.

Recreation Manager Manisco stated the Aquatics RFQ review panel had six
members and staff reviewed the submitted proposals and the final grading sheets.

Vice Chair Lingo encouraged the Commission to trust Staff and their
recommendation on the RFQ process.

In response to Chair Villablanca, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the
Commission did not request to approve the selected contractor following the
Aquatics RFQ process.

Vice Chair Lingo stated the RFQ specified that an interview would be conducted if
needed.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Administrative Assistant Saleaumua stated the
Aquatics vendor had a three-year agreement, with the option to extend for one year,
for an additional three years, for a total of six years.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated the Commission chose not to be involved in the RFQ process, but the Ad
Hoc Committee was crucial in assisting the Department with meeting with each
Swim Team prior to the decision to release the RFQ.

In response to Chair Villablanca, Commissioner Peak stated that Commissioner
Skophammer and herself served on the Ad Hoc Committee and tried to help resolve
pool usage between two Swim Team groups, which resulted in unresolvable
cooperation. She stated due to the conflict, the Commission decided to create an
RFQ process.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated that a proposal checklist and signature line could be added to the RFQ
application.

Commissioner Peak stated that she wanted staff to exercise due diligence in the
future to confirm that all submitted information was accurate.

Chair Villablanca suggested applicants provide proof of certification.

  Malibu Bluffs Park Outdoor Fitness Equipment Proiect
  Recommended Action: l) Review outdoor fitness equipment options for Malibu
  Bluffs Park; and 2) Provide feedback regarding the design.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the current
  pour—in-place material at the workout station area would be replaced.

  Vice Chair Lingo stated the replacement workout station looked great.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated he was not in favor of the cardio walker
  equipment.

  Commissioner Peak preferred youth climbing equipment rather than a second
  workout station.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Community Services Director Riesgo stated taller
  climbing equipment would be for children 5 to 12 years old.

  Recreation Manager Manisco stated the Commission provided feedback during the
  December 9, 2025 Special meeting to add a workout station in the vacant
  playground area.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the proposed workout station in the vacant
  playground area should be a different design.

  The Commission indicated agreement.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented a climbing apparatus design for the vacant
  playground area.

  The Commission recommended staff research climbing apparatus options for
  children 5 to 12 years old.

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Vice Chair Lingo seconded a motion to approve the
  proposed workout station design to replace the workout station destroyed in the
  Broad Fire and recommended staff to research a climbing apparatus for the vacant
  playground area. The Commission recommended blue pour-in-place surface. The
  question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Commissioner Goldfarb absent.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on Senior programs.
   Parks and Recreation Commission

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the Community Lands
  Project, Snack Shack and Enhancement Project, and Skate Park.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Peak requested to agendize the Las Flores Creek Dog Park.

  Chair Villablanca requested to hold a meeting at Las Flores Creek Park to discuss
  the feasibility of installing a Dog Park.

  In response to Commissioner Peak. Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  community members should notify City staff if people were trespassing in the Skate
  Park. She stated the City had security patrolling Malibu Bluffs Park and Legacy
  Park, and officers would help staffenforce the park rules.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Las Flores Creek Dog Park

ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Villablanca adjourned the meeting at 8:30 p.m.
